clue.text: Bellows creation recalls Colonel Bramble's creator

definitions.text: Bellows creation recalls Colonel Bramble's creator

parts.words: Bellows creation recalls Colonel Bramble's creator
parts.note: Saul Bellow's novel hero Moses Herzog brings to mind the French author born Emile Herzog, who wrote The Silence of Colonel Bramble under a pen name

explanation.surface: A character from a Saul Bellow novel puts the reader in mind of a French novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellow's Herzog is the link: the writer of Les Silences du Colonel Bramble was born Emile Herzog and took his pen name from a French village.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist and biographer wrote Les Silences du Colonel Bramble in 1918, about British officers in the Great War.

clue.text: Agatha Christie built a better one

definitions.text: Agatha Christie built a better one

parts.words: Agatha Christie built a better one
parts.note: plays on the proverb that the world beats a path to the door of whoever builds a better rodent catcher, and on Christie's record-running stage play

explanation.surface: The crime writer improved on a familiar household gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says 'build a better mousetrap and the world will beat a path to your door'; Christie's play of that name has run in London since 1952.
explanation.definitionFit: Christie's stage thriller of that title is the longest-running play in theatre history, and the proverbial invention in the saying.

clue.text: His are all sound and fury, signify ing nothing " (C. Bronté, Shirley)

definitions.text: His are all sound and fury, signify ing nothing " (C. Bronté, Shirley)

parts.words: His are all sound and fury, signify ing nothing " (C. Bronté, Shirley)
parts.note: a quotation from Charlotte Bronte's novel with a gap after His; the missing noun is the loud outbursts that echo Macbeth's sound and fury

explanation.surface: A line from Shirley, borrowing Macbeth's words about a tale told by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: A gap-fill clue: the blank falls between 'His' and 'are' in the quoted line.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy tumults and outcries are exactly what 'sound and fury' describes in Shakespeare's phrase that Bronte borrows.

clue.text: Sir John Davies poem said to be banned, upmarket

definitions.meaning: Davies's 1596 poem on dancing bears this title
a musical band sounds like banned when spoken, and a large ensemble of players is a band
in American theatres the front stalls, the dearest seats, bear this name

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan poem is supposedly prohibited, yet still posh.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the poem 'Orchestra, or a Poem of Dancing'; 'banned' sounds like 'band'; and the front stalls of a US theatre, the expensive seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Davies's poem has that title; a symphony ensemble is a band; and the costly ground-floor theatre seats carry the same name in American usage.

clue.text: Dismiss Falstaff's tipple

definitions.meaning: to fire someone from a job
Falstaff drinks sherris-..., a dry Spanish white wine, throughout Henry IV

explanation.surface: Get rid of the fat knight's favourite drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire an employee is to give them the boot; Shakespeare's Falstaff praises the fortified wine called sack at length.

clue.text: Coward's were red

parts.note: Noel Coward wrote a one-act play in Tonight at 8.30 titled Red ___, about a pair of music-hall performers

explanation.surface: Something belonging to a timid person was coloured red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person, but it is Noel Coward, whose short play is 'Red Peppers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward's one-act comedy in the Tonight at 8.30 cycle is called Red Peppers.

clue.text: Those who sample US poet are versifiers

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe is the American poet
people who sample food or wine are tasters

explanation.surface: People who dip into an American poet's work turn out to write verse themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of feeble or second-rate verse are rhymesters, a dismissive word for versifiers.

clue.text: "But came the tide, and made my his prey" (Spenser, Amoretti)

definitions.text: "But came the tide, and made my his prey" (Spenser, Amoretti)

parts.words: "But came the tide, and made my his prey" (Spenser, Amoretti)
parts.note: Spenser's sonnet 75 has the poet writing his love's name on the sand, and the gap after my is the efforts the waves wash away

explanation.surface: A line from Spenser's sonnet about a name written on the strand.
explanation.walkthrough: A gap-fill clue: the missing word falls between 'my' and 'his' in Amoretti 75.
explanation.definitionFit: In the sonnet the sea washes away the poet's careful efforts, the trouble he took writing her name.

clue.text: A grave, but positive, review

parts.note: a tombstone inscription sums up a life, usually kindly, so it is a review written for a grave

explanation.surface: A serious yet favourable critique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' reads as 'serious', but it is the burial place where the kind summing-up is carved.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombstone inscription assesses the dead, and custom keeps it flattering.

clue.text: Mason didn't spell Miss Wong's name thus (one could make an issue of it)

definitions.text: Mason didn't spell Miss Wong's name thus

indicators.note: one could rearrange the word issue to make another word, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Richard Mason spelt his heroine's name differently, and the alternative could cause a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Mason's novel is The World of Suzie Wong, with a Z; this spelling uses S. 'could make an' signals the anagram of ISSUE; 'of it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's title character is Suzie, so the S-spelling is the version Mason avoided.

clue.text: Plentiful riches may obscure militant saint

indicators.note: the plentiful riches hide the run of letters inside them, concealing it from view

explanation.surface: Great wealth can hide a fighting holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulrich of Augsburg, a tenth-century bishop canonised as a saint, led the defence of his city against the Magyar invaders.

clue.text: CIA clue is interpreted to reveal immigrant Roman playwright

indicators.note: an interpreted clue is worked out and rendered differently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US intelligence agency deciphers a hint pointing to a Roman dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Caecilius Statius came to Rome from Gaul as a slave, hence 'immigrant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caecilius Statius, a comic dramatist of the second century BC, was a Gallic captive who settled in Rome.

clue.text: Wiped out for long periods by editor

parts.note: an era is a long period of history

explanation.surface: Something deleted over many years by a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete or rub out something completely is to obliterate it.

clue.text: Barsetshire character in Hawthorne work

definitions.meaning: a figure in the novels set in the fictional English county of Barsetshire
Nathaniel Hawthorne's first novel, published anonymously in 1828

explanation.surface: A Trollope-land figure turns up in an American novelist's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Barsetshire is the fictional English county of Trollope's novels, later revived by Angela Thirkell; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to a Barsetshire family and is the title of Hawthorne's early college romance.

clue.text: Dean's in-law might be an austere sectarian

indicators.note: the letters of the words could be rearranged into something else, so they are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter
taken as written, the hyphen giving no letter

explanation.surface: A dean's relative by marriage could belong to a severe religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: The followers of Peter Waldo were a medieval Christian movement known for poverty and plain living.

clue.text: Change typeface, for example, or in another direction

definitions.meaning: a printer changing type has to compose the page again
to point or fix something again, set to a new direction

explanation.surface: Alter the font, or turn the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Composing type afresh means setting it again; aligning something a new way is setting it again too.

clue.text: You and me at California resort for Seleucid king

parts.note: Antioch is a town in northern California
you and me together make us

explanation.surface: Two people at a West Coast holiday spot meet an ancient monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings of the Seleucid dynasty of Syria bore this name, the best known being Antiochus the Great.

clue.text: Former pupil meeting is magnificent in Douglas

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a session is a sitting or meeting

explanation.surface: An old boy's gathering is splendid on the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas looks like the Manx capital, but it is Lloyd C. Douglas, whose novel is Magnificent Obsession; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd C. Douglas's 1929 bestseller was titled Magnificent Obsession, so the missing word follows magnificent.

clue.text: Sara Monday thus taken unawares

definitions.meaning: Sara Monday narrates Joyce Cary's novel Herself ___

explanation.surface: Sara Monday was caught napping.
explanation.walkthrough: Sara Monday is the narrator of Joyce Cary's novel Herself Surprised (1941).
explanation.definitionFit: Cary's heroine appears in Herself Surprised; to be caught unawares is to be startled.

clue.text: Pier performance and hospital series for a Greek sage

indicators.note: a performance puts on a show, here making the letters of pier put on a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
ER is the American television drama set in a hospital emergency room

explanation.surface: A seaside show and a medical drama lead to an ancient philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Periander, tyrant of Corinth, was counted among the Seven Sages of ancient Greece.

clue.text: What play's new version does to original plot

definitions.text: What play's new version does to original plot

parts.words: What play's new version does to original plot
parts.note: an adaptation tells the old story over again

explanation.surface: A remake of a drama handles the source story.
explanation.definitionFit: A reworking narrates the same story once more.

clue.text: Plead for some new art centre attractions

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are taken, a run lying inside it

explanation.surface: Appeal for a few new exhibits at the art centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech or beg someone earnestly is to plead with them.

clue.text: Scene of Graeco-Turkish struggle -met in Ely, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A Greek-Turkish conflict apparently took place in a Cambridgeshire cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mytilene on Lesbos was fought over by Greeks and Ottoman Turks, falling to the Greeks in 1912.

clue.text: Strange feature of queen, appreciated by Polonius

definitions.text: Strange feature of queen, appreciated by Polonius

parts.words: Strange feature of queen, appreciated by Polonius
parts.note: in Hamlet the player speaks of the muffled Hecuba, and Polonius approves the odd adjective as good

explanation.surface: Polonius admires an odd trait of a royal lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet II.ii: the player says 'the mobled queen', and Polonius comments "'Mobled queen' is good".
explanation.definitionFit: The rare word, meaning muffled or veiled, describes Hecuba in the player's speech, and Polonius praises it.

clue.text: True as Southerne's sibling

definitions.meaning: Thomas Southerne's 1682 tragedy is The ___ Brother

explanation.surface: Faithful, like the dramatist's brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful and steadfast are synonyms of true; Southerne's first play was The Loyal Brother.

clue.text: Love goddess in newish tartan dress

indicators.note: the goddess is found inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A goddess of love wears a new plaid outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' is a link word that completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Babylonian deity of love and war was worshipped across Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Wodehouse relative made seasonal appearance

parts.note: P G Wodehouse's uncle character, Lord Ickenham, appears in a novel titled Uncle ___ in the Springtime

explanation.surface: A family member in a comic novel shows up at a particular time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Wodehouse's Uncle Fred, Lord Ickenham, stars in Uncle Fred in the Springtime (1939).

clue.text: Pork pie producer on goat in Waterhouse work

indicators.note: in an across clue, the second piece is placed on, that is after, the first

parts.note: a male goat is a billy
pork pies are lies in Cockney rhyming slang, so one who produces them is a teller of falsehoods

explanation.surface: A butcher's pie-maker sits on a goat in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'pork pies' means 'lies'. Keith Waterhouse wrote the 1959 novel Billy Liar; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Waterhouse's comic novel about a daydreaming Yorkshire clerk is Billy Liar.

clue.text: Notions for Drayton's Mirrour

definitions.meaning: Michael Drayton's 1594 sonnet sequence is titled ___ Mirrour

explanation.surface: Thoughts for an Elizabethan sonnet sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts are concepts; Drayton's sonnets appeared as Idea's Mirrour, addressed to his ideal lady.

clue.text: Piles on difficulty in an excerpt from Creek letters

indicators.note: the words are in difficulty, in trouble, so their letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A heap of trouble arises from a passage in some Greek letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet is one item taken from that alphabet.

clue.text: Presented academic on wrong date

indicators.note: the scrambled letters follow, placed on, the first piece

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: the word date is wrongly arranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A university lecturer turned up on the wrong day.
explanation.definitionFit: Gave as a gift, as a donor gives to a charity.
